newsitem.title: INDIA: India April wheat stocks at 3.24 million tonnes.
newsitem.headline: India April wheat stocks at 3.24 million tonnes.

text.p: India, as on April 1, 1997, held wheat stocks of 3.24 million tonnes, lower than government's minimum buffer stock norm of 3.7 million, Food and Agriculture Minister Chaturanan Mishra said on Friday.
Mishra told parliament that India held 7.76 million tonnes of wheat stocks on the same date in 1996.
The government buys wheat to build up its buffer stocks, which it then uses to control prices by releasing stocks through a state-run distribution system.
Mishra said up to May 8 state procurement agencies had bought 3.83 million tonnes of wheat from farmers, compared with 6.49 million tonnes at the same time last year.
Mishra said unseasonal rains in April had delayed wheat procurement operations.
"Agitation by a certain section of farmers demanding higher minimum support prices for wheat also affected the arrival of wheat in the markets to some extent," Mishra said.

He said India in December 1996, decided to import up to two million tonnes of wheat in 1996/97 (April-March), out of which the state-run State Trading Corp (STC) had contracted to import 1.68 million tonnes.
About 1.47 million tonnes of wheat had already arrived in India by May 2, Mishra said.
Out of the 1.68 million tonnes contracted to be imported in 1996/97, 1.33 million was contracted from Australia, 250,000 tonnes from Canada and 100,000 tonnes from Argentina.
Mishra said India had also decided to import an additional two million tonnes in 1997/98. Out of this STC had contracted to import one million tonnes.
Mishra said wheat output in 1996/97 (July-June) was expected to be about 64.66 million tonnes, about two million tonnes more than the production in 1995/96.
"Production of wheat during the current year and also the imports of wheat during the year are likely to meet the demand of the country," Mishra said.
